text:
Running a 3B parameter model directly on a mid-range Android device used to feel like an exercise in thermal throttling. But recent optimizations in ExecuTorch and 4-bit quantization are changing what is practical on edge hardware.

The main issue with local inference on mobile has never been raw compute speed. It is unified memory bandwidth and battery power. When an unoptimized runtime pegs the GPU, thermal management throttles your core frequencies within two minutes.

By shifting matrix multiplication to dedicated NPUs and keeping weight sizes under 2GB, offline background tasks suddenly become viable. You get zero network latency, total data privacy, and zero API costs per user.

The trade-off is precision. Drops in output quality are real when compressing weights down to INT4, especially for complex reasoning tasks. But for structured text extraction or quick classification, local models are ready for production.

Are you testing local LLMs on mobile yet, or are API calls still the default for your stack?
